tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
schema.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key' and the volume buttons: how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

When run_in_terminal or open_terminal_tab opens a new tab, pass cwd as a full absolute path.

lines: +## 2026-11-28 Hosted browser settings were absent from the compiled renderer (BOARDROOM_VITE_ENV_FILTER)

+- **Evidence:** The production build log showed the hosted-browser feature enabled and its public health probe passing, but the real UI still displayed the external-open card. Both Vite environment-prefix lists omitted `VITE_BOARDROOM_BROWSER_`. A compiler-level regression reproduced the omission: with enabled=true, the emitted module exported enabled=false.

+- **Fix:** Allow the public browser-settings prefix in both renderer build configurations. The Hosting build now runs a test that compiles the actual endpoint resolver with each configuration and checks both enabled and explicitly disabled output.

+- **Prevention:** A CI environment value and a healthy worker do not prove that Vite exposed the configuration to the browser. Verify the emitted endpoint and then test the genuine signed-in UI. Deploy matching worker sources before accepting new client capabilities.
## 2026-11-27 Healthy Boardroom worker fell back to blocked iframes

- **Cause:** The Studio build supplied a WebSocket origin while the renderer required the `/boardroom` path. An HTTP 200 from `/health` hid the mismatch. The fallback embedded sites that forbid framing, and the hosted worker accepted only two portal hosts.

Generated from an import-reachability scan of `packages/renderer/src` (roots: `src/main.tsx`, `src/startupWatchdog.ts`, workers; aliases `@/`, `@agents/`, `@shared/`, `@indii/shared`; dynamic `import()`, `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` and `import.meta.glob` followed). Each file below is imported by **nothing** — not the app, not tests, not storybook, not other packages, not build config. TypeSafe Jev (`jev-latest`) classified each one; it labelled these as finished-looking features that were never wired in, so they are a product decision rather than safe cleanup.

Tracking: `.agent/test_ledger/OPEN_ISSUES_V4.md` ISSUE-1726. Batch 1 (21 unused helpers/duplicates, ISSUE-1725) is already removed.

**Decide per row (109 files, ~13.6k lines):** wire it in, or delete it. Rows marked † import each other, so delete them together.

Not listed here (separate decisions, same scan):
- 110 files / ~17.6k lines reachable **only from tests**, plus ~94 test files (~10k lines) that exist only to test them.
- 36 of 97 judgments in `config/typesafeJudgments.ts` (~4.7k lines) with no production caller.
- ~3.5k lines of copies of `packages/shared` code in `renderer` and `firebase` (foundry, DDEX types, subscription tiers, creative schemas) that should import `@indii/shared`.
- ~152 MB of tracked non-code: `archive/`, `ft_export/`, `artifacts/`, `videos/` (one 24 MB WAV is stored twice).

Kept on purpose (not candidates): `services/web3/**` (deferred infrastructure), `*.d.ts` ambient types, fixtures, storybook, `config/i18n.ts`, and files referenced from outside the renderer.

== 7148402f0
refactor(ui): remove dead controls, dedupe twin panels, wire dead-end CTAs (ISSUE-1441)
Delete the StudioControlsPanel mock blocks (CAMERA MOVEMENT buttons had no
onClick, FPS bar was decorative, Shot List was mock) leaving only the wired
motion slider. Unregister the deprecated revenue_mtd/revenue_aggregated
dashboard widgets entirely — migrateWidgets still upgrades persisted boards
carrying the legacy ids onto revenue_consolidated. Delete publishing's drifted
DistributorConnectionsPanel and EarningsDashboard forks in favor of the
canonical distribution/finance originals, and drop distribution's duplicate
Founder Readiness tab (RegistrationCenter is its single home). Wire the
dashboard's dead-end CTAs: Initialize Release -> distribution, Connect
Storefront -> merch.

 .../components/DistributorConnectionsPanel.tsx     |  71 ---------
 .../publishing/components/EarningsDashboard.tsx    | 133 ----------------
 .../PublishingEarningsDashboard.test.tsx           |  29 ----
== 01a72211a
refactor(registry): delete orphaned UI code, remove phantom module ids, fix registry defects (ISSUE-1442)
UI-first backwards redundancy audit, Stage 1 + 1b (map: docs/REDUNDANCY_AUDIT_UI_FIRST.md).

Stage 1 — provably dead code (~2,900 LOC, zero behavior change):
- Delete unregistered orphan modules modules/royalty (0 imports) and
  modules/design (+ its exclusive consumer services/design).
- Delete zero-consumer services: ai (dead shim; verify-ai-features.ts now
  imports the canonical intelligence facade), daw, education, monitoring,
  optimistic, config, firebase-guards.ts.
- Merge services/blockchain into services/web3: live SmartContractService +
  IPFSPinataService move; duplicate OpenSeaService and zero-consumer
  ENSIdentityService deleted; merch imports rewired.
- Remove phantom id audio-analyzer end to end (component 621 LOC, tests,
  lazy chunk, registry, colors, theme, agent map, org-access list, skill
  registry, loading fallbacks, appSlice rewrite; CommandPad hub card now
  targets analytics). Legacy /audio-analyzer URLs still redirect via
  useURLSync ROUTE_ALIASES; persisted ids fail isValidModule and fall back
  to dashboard (existing store hydration guard).
- Remove phantom id format-foundry registration; its component is ALIVE as
  the Finance forensics tab, so it relocates to modules/finance/components/
  (services/foundry untouched — agent tools consume it).
- Delete zero-importer modules/tools/MIDIController and SonicRadar
  (TagMatrix stays: consumed by Distribution QCPanel).

Stage 1b — registry/usefulness defects:
- Wire the PROJECT_CANVAS flag into GATED_MODULES (it existed with a
  dev-only default but gated nothing — module shipped to prod regardless).
- Add 15 missing MODULE_DISPLAY_NAMES entries (h1 fell back to raw ids).
- Add registration + security to the mobile More drawer (unreachable on
  phones without ⌘K).
- Remove dead sidebar history archives branch; fix screenwriter/crm cssVar
  raw-HSL values that produced invalid var() CSS.

Silent-revert justification: the removed appSlice alias block and the
format-foundry registration were the documented subject of ISSUE-1436/
1437/1438 cleanups; this completes their direction. Ledger: ISSUE-1442.

Validation: renderer tsc 0 errors (touched files); 129 tests green across
14 affected suites; eslint 0 errors; build:studio green; check-test-quality
0 violations.

feat(perf): slim App.tsx router and simplify modulePreload filters (ISSUE-549 §2, §3)

4355:### ISSUE-1721: Creative Studio chat fails `"hi"` with `Failed to get document because the client is offline.` and fails message persistence while showing `ONLINE`
4376:### ISSUE-1722: Boardroom rail and drawer layout spec remainder (WP7 L2–L5)

4392:### ISSUE-1724: Unused Boardroom UI files and dead browser history export (WP12)
### ISSUE-1726: Decide wire-or-delete for 109 never-imported renderer files (dead-code batch 2)

- **Status:** 🔴 OPEN (2026-11-28 — awaiting William's pick per file)
- **Severity:** 🟢 LOW
- **Module:** `packages/renderer/src` — list in `docs/plans/dead-code-candidates-2026-11-28.md` (~13.6k lines; largest: `services/agent/memory/MemorySearch.ts`, `IntelligenceEnhancePostModal.tsx`, `SchedulerStatusPanel.tsx`, `AgentContextBridge.ts`, `TerritoryRightsPanel.tsx`)
- **Context:** Jev labelled these as finished-looking features never wired in, so per the YAGNI/find-use-cases rule they are not deleted automatically. The same doc lists the follow-on batches: test-only-reachable files (~17.6k lines + ~10k lines of their tests), 36 uncalled judgments in `config/typesafeJudgments.ts` (~4.7k lines), `packages/shared` copies (~3.5k lines), and ~152 MB of tracked non-code.
- **Depends on:** ISSUE-1725 (merge batch 1 first so the scan baseline is current).
- **Acceptance:** Every row in the doc is either wired in (with a reachable import from `src/main.tsx`) or deleted; re-run the reachability scan and confirm zero files imported by nothing outside the documented keep list.
- **SEVERITY:** High (the Road Director — the flagship touring agent — could never search places or compute distances even though the secured backend and provisioned keys existed; the user-visible Planning map silently ignored new waypoints)
- **FILES:** `packages/renderer/src/services/agent/tools/MapsTools.ts`, `packages/firebase/src/lib/touring.ts`, `packages/firebase/src/index.ts`, `packages/renderer/src/services/agent/definitions/{RoadAgent,HospitalityAgent,EventPlannerAgent}.ts`, `packages/renderer/src/modules/touring/RoadManager.tsx`, `packages/renderer/src/modules/touring/components/PlanningTab.tsx`, `packages/renderer/src/modules/touring/hooks/useTouring.ts`, `packages/renderer/src/services/touring/TouringService.ts`, `agents/road/prompt.md`
- **ERROR:** Two failures, one chat. (1) `MapsTools` returned `MAPS_BROWSER_DISABLED` unconditionally for `search_places`/`get_place_details`/`get_distance_matrix` — a deliberate fail-closed from the 2026-08-09 "declarations are contracts" hardening that was never revisited after `findPlaces` (auth + App Check + `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` secret) shipped and the 2026-08-18 audit proved Geocoding/Places live with CI-injected keys. The Road Director therefore honestly-but-uselessly answered "not authorized — configure the Google Maps API key in global settings" (there is no such in-app setting; the model improvised the guidance). `get_distance_matrix` additionally had NO backend at all. (2) In PlanningTab, the map's `locations` prop bound to the SAVED itinerary stops whenever one existed, so newly added waypoints never rendered while the "Total Waypoints" overlay counted the unsaved array — counter said 3, map showed 2. After reload the editor reset to "No waypoints added" while the map kept rendering the previous draft's stops. import re
base = 'packages/renderer/src/modules/dashboard/components/'
p = base + 'CustomDashboardWidgets.tsx'
s = open(p).read()

start = s.index("export type WidgetType =")
end = s.index("export const DEFAULT_WIDGETS")
block = s[start:end]
s = s[:start] + (
    "export type { WidgetType, Widget } from '@/modules/dashboard/components/dashboardWidgetDefinitions';\n"
    "export { WIDGET_DEFINITIONS } from '@/modules/dashboard/components/dashboardWidgetDefinitions';\n\n"
) + s[end:]

imp_anchor = "import { WidgetEmptyState } from '@/modules/dashboard/components/WidgetEmptyState';"
assert imp_anchor in s
s = s.replace(imp_anchor, imp_anchor + "\n"
    "import type { WidgetType, Widget } from '@/modules/dashboard/components/dashboardWidgetDefinitions';\n"
    "import RecentProjects from '@/modules/dashboard/components/RecentProjects';\n"
    "import StatsRibbon from '@/modules/dashboard/components/StatsRibbon';\n"
    "import { DataStorageManager } from '@/modules/dashboard/components/DataStorageManager';\n"
    "import { KnowledgeBaseList } from '@/modules/dashboard/components/KnowledgeBaseList';", 1)

r_anchor = "    cost_estimator: () => <CostEstimatorWidget />,\n};"
assert r_anchor in s
s = s.replace(r_anchor, "    cost_estimator: () => <CostEstimatorWidget />,\n"
    "    recent_projects: () => <RecentProjects />,\n"
    "    workspace_stats: () => <StatsRibbon />,\n"
    "    storage_usage: () => <DataStorageManager />,\n"
    "    knowledge_base: () => <KnowledgeBaseList />,\n};", 1)
open(p, 'w').write(s)

# definitions module
block = block.replace("export const WIDGET_DEFINITIONS", "export const WIDGET_DEFINITIONS", 1)
block = block.replace("    | 'cost_estimator';", "    | 'cost_estimator'\n    | 'recent_projects'\n    | 'workspace_stats'\n    | 'storage_usage'\n    | 'knowledge_base';", 1)
block = block.replace("    cost_estimator: { label: 'Cost Estimator', icon: DollarSign, description: 'Estimate generation costs' },",
    "    cost_estimator: { label: 'Cost Estimator', icon: DollarSign, description: 'Estimate generation costs' },\n"
    "    recent_projects: { label: 'Recent Projects', icon: FolderOpen, description: 'Jump back into your latest projects or start a new one' },\n"
    "    workspace_stats: { label: 'Workspace Stats', icon: Layers, description: 'Projects, agent conversations, and storage at a glance' },\n"
    "    storage_usage: { label: 'Storage', icon: HardDrive, description: 'How your storage splits across images, video, and knowledge files' },\n"
    "    knowledge_base: { label: 'Knowledge Base', icon: BookOpen, description: 'Documents you have added for your team to reference' },", 1)
icons = sorted(set(re.findall(r"icon: (\w+)", block)))
header = ("import type { LucideIcon } from 'lucide-react';\n"
          f"import {{ {', '.join(icons)} }} from 'lucide-react';\n\n"
          "/**\n * Dashboard widget types and their picker metadata.\n"
          " * Renderers live in CustomDashboardWidgets.tsx (WIDGET_RENDERERS).\n */\n")
open(base + 'dashboardWidgetDefinitions.ts', 'w').write(header + block.rstrip() + "\n")
print(icons)

content.text:
Everything is installed and 9 of the unconnected files are now wired into the app, pushed to branch `claude/wire-unconnected-w1`. I haven't checked them in the logged-in app, and the remote CI hasn't run.

**Install:** the 3D libraries that were missing are now installed with an isolated cache, and the lockfile didn't change. The full `npm run typecheck` now passes on `main`.

**Wired in:**
- **Observability dashboard:**
  - Added the agent budget panel. It used to show "Healthy" when the budget service was unreachable; now it shows "Status Unavailable". An unlimited budget now reads "Unlimited" instead of "$Infinity".
  - Added the scheduler status panel.
- **Settings:**
  - Appearance now has a language picker that switches the app between English and Spanish.
  - The web version's Desktop section now has a desktop app download card. It links to the same release source the desktop updater uses, and I removed its "Founder Exclusive" label because nothing backs it.
- **Home dashboard:** four new widgets you can add from the widget picker: Recent Projects, Workspace Stats, Storage and Knowledge Base. All four show live data, and the default layout is unchanged.
- The import scan confirms all 9 files are now reachable from the app.
- The typecheck, lint (no errors), affected tests (86 passed, including new tests for the budget panel, language picker and widget list), production build, file-size check and ledger checks all pass.

**Not wired yet:** nine files would have become controls that do nothing or mislead you:
- **Theme toggle:** no light theme exists, so it would change nothing.
- **"Do not sell my data" toggle:** nothing reads the setting, so it would promise an opt-out that doesn't happen.
- **Territory rights panel:** release delivery ignores territory splits.
- **Session timeout screen:** any click dismisses it, so it isn't a real lock.
- **Five other files:** an older copy of something that already ships in the app.

The reason for each is recorded in the ledger as ISSUE-1727.

**What's left:** the remaining ~90 files are sorted by readiness in `docs/plans/wire-in-map-2026-11-28.md` on the branch. Jev's sorting is only a hint: it was unsure about most files and wrong on the ones I checked, so I check each file myself before wiring it.

**Don't merge `claude/prune-unreachable-renderer`.** That branch deletes 20 helper files, which contradicts keeping everything.

Should I wire the next batch of files the map marks ready (error reporting, the local helper status indicator, community webhooks, Veo video settings, the organization picker), or would you rather review the map first?

content.text:
I went with privacy first, since it's a legal requirement: Settings now has a Privacy section, and the "Do Not Sell or Share" opt-out actually does something. It's pushed to `claude/wire-unconnected-w1`, which brings the total to 15 previously unconnected files now wired into the app. I haven't tried it in the logged-in app, and the remote CI hasn't run.

**What changed:**
- **Error reports you can switch off later:** until now you could only choose once, in the cookie banner. The Privacy section lets you change that any time, and turning it off stops crash reporting and session recording immediately.
- **The opt-out is enforced, not just saved:**
  - It's stored on your account and applied on the device right away.
  - It blocks any analytics or marketing sharing.
  - Error reports no longer include your email or IP address.
  - The wording now says plainly that indii does not sell personal information, which is true.
- **Under the hood:**
  - Consent settings now live in one service shared by the cookie banner, error reporting and Settings, instead of inside the banner component.
  - The settings on/off switches now work with screen readers.

All checks pass: typecheck, lint, 886 tests across the affected areas (including new tests showing the email is removed and reporting stops when you opt out), the code-quality checks and the production build.

**Not done yet: results for the existing-files import hub.** The backend already analyzes uploaded tracks, but users can't see the results yet. That needs a database security rule so only the owner can read their own results, plus a screen that lists them. I stopped before writing it because a security-rule change should be tested against the local Firebase emulator first, and I haven't run that here.

**Left as they are, my call:** organization switching stays limited to dev builds, since most indie artists run one organization. A light theme is a design project, so it waits.

Should I build the import results next (the owner-only rule tested on the emulator, plus the results screen), or pause here so you can review and merge what's on the branch?
